# Component Mounting Positional Deviation Measurement Unit

## Overview and Installation

A component mounting positional deviation amount measurement unit is provided for installation in the feeder setting section of a component mounting machine. This measurement unit is specifically designed with dimensional and structural compatibility that allows it to be installed interchangeably with a standard cassette-type feeder. This exchangeability ensures that the measurement unit can be easily inserted into the same setting section used for production feeders, without requiring modifications to the component mounting machine itself. As a result, positional deviation measurement can be performed using the existing feeder setting infrastructure whenever calibration or diagnostic verification is required, and the measurement unit can subsequently be removed to restore normal production operation with cassette-type feeders.

## Structural Components of the Measurement Unit

The measurement unit incorporates several key functional sections that work together to enable accurate positional deviation measurement:

**Measurement Nozzle Placement Sections**
The unit includes dedicated placement sections designed to hold measurement nozzles. These measurement nozzles are configured to be exchangeably mounted onto the mounting head of the component mounting machine, similar to how production nozzles are attached during normal operation. This exchangeable mounting capability allows the mounting head to retrieve a measurement nozzle from the measurement unit in the same manner it would retrieve a standard production nozzle.

**Measurement Component Placement Sections**
The measurement unit also contains placement sections specifically for holding measurement components. These measurement components serve as reference parts that are used during the measurement process, taking the place of actual production components.

**Measurement Mounting Table with Fiducial Mark**
A measurement mounting table is integrated into the unit, and this table is equipped with a measurement fiducial mark. This fiducial mark serves as a precise positional reference point against which the accuracy of component placement can be evaluated.

## Measurement Procedure

The process for measuring component mounting positional deviation proceeds as follows:

1. **Nozzle Acquisition**: The mounting head of the component mounting machine first moves to the measurement nozzle placement section and picks up a measurement nozzle, mounting it onto the head in an exchangeable manner.

2. **Component Pickup**: Using the newly attached measurement nozzle, the mounting head then moves to the measurement component placement section and picks up a measurement component.

3. **Component Mounting**: The mounting head subsequently transports the measurement component to the measurement mounting table and places it onto the table surface, in proximity to the measurement fiducial mark.

## Calculation of Positional Deviation

Once the measurement component has been mounted onto the measurement mounting table, the actual position of the placed component is compared against the measurement fiducial mark. The offset, or discrepancy, between the position of the mounted measurement component and the reference position indicated by the fiducial mark is measured and calculated. This offset value directly represents the positional deviation amount of the component mounting machine, providing a quantitative measure of the machine's placement accuracy. This measured deviation can then be used to assess whether the mounting machine requires calibration adjustments to maintain precise component placement during actual production runs.

# Component Mounting Positional Deviation Measurement Unit

## Overview

The component mounting positional deviation measurement unit represents an innovative approach to evaluating and calibrating the positional accuracy of component mounting machines used in electronics manufacturing. This unit is specifically engineered to be interchangeable with a standard cassette-type feeder, allowing it to be installed directly into the feeder setting section of a component mounting machine without requiring specialized modifications to the machine itself. This interchangeability is a key design feature, as it enables manufacturers to perform accuracy assessments using the same physical infrastructure and setup procedures already established for normal production operations.

## Structural Configuration

The measurement unit incorporates several essential structural elements that work together to facilitate the measurement process:

**Placement Sections for Measurement Nozzles**: The unit includes dedicated sections where measurement nozzles are stored and made available for retrieval by the mounting head. These nozzles are specialized tools designed specifically for the measurement process, distinct from the nozzles used during standard component placement operations.

**Placement Sections for Measurement Components**: Similarly, the unit provides designated areas for holding measurement components—reference components used exclusively for accuracy testing rather than actual production. These components serve as the physical medium through which positional data is captured.

**Measurement Mounting Table with Fiducial Mark**: Perhaps the most critical structural feature is the measurement mounting table, which incorporates a fiducial mark. This fiducial mark serves as a fixed, precisely known reference point against which the actual placement position of the measurement component can be compared. The fiducial mark essentially establishes the "ground truth" coordinate against which any positional deviation is calculated.

## Operational Process

The measurement procedure follows a systematic sequence that mirrors the standard component mounting workflow, thereby providing a realistic assessment of the machine's actual operational accuracy:

1. **Nozzle Pickup**: The mounting head of the component mounting machine first retrieves a measurement nozzle from its designated placement section within the measurement unit.

2. **Component Suction**: Using the acquired measurement nozzle, the mounting head then performs a suction operation to pick up a measurement component from its corresponding placement section.

3. **Component Mounting**: The mounting head proceeds to mount the measurement component onto the measurement mounting table, following the same motion and placement logic used in standard production mounting operations.

4. **Deviation Measurement**: Once the measurement component has been placed on the table, its position relative to the fiducial mark is measured. Any discrepancy between the intended placement position and the actual placement position—as indicated by its offset from the fiducial mark—represents the positional deviation of the mounting machine.

## Practical Significance

This integrated methodology offers several practical advantages for manufacturers and quality control processes. Because the measurement unit is designed to be interchangeable with existing feeder infrastructure, it can be seamlessly incorporated into regular maintenance and calibration schedules without necessitating additional specialized equipment or extensive machine downtime. Furthermore, by utilizing the actual mounting head and replicating the genuine pick up-and-place sequence, the measurement process captures real-world positional accuracy data that reflects the machine's true performance characteristics, rather than relying on theoretical or indirect assessment methods.

This approach thereby provides manufacturers with a practical, efficient, and reliable technique for quantifying the positional accuracy of their component mounting machines, supporting quality assurance efforts and enabling timely identification of any accuracy degradation that may require corrective calibration.

# When

"When" is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it carries an enormous weight of meaning. It is the word we reach for whenever we want to locate something in time—a question that has occupied human thought since we first became aware of our own mortality.

Children ask "when" almost as soon as they learn to speak: When will we get there? When is my birthday? When will you be back? The question reveals an innate human need to understand not just what will happen, but the shape and rhythm of time itself.

Philosophers and physicists have spent centuries debating what "when" really means. Is time a river flowing in one direction, carrying us along whether we like it or not? Or is it something more flexible, relative to our position and speed, as Einstein suggested? For most of us in daily life, though, "when" simply means the practical business of scheduling, waiting, remembering, and anticipating.

There is something bittersweet about the word. "When I was young..." carries nostalgia. "When you're ready..." carries patience and possibility. "When will this end?" can carry weariness or hope, depending on the context. A single syllable, and yet it can hold grief, excitement, uncertainty, or promise.

In storytelling, "when" often marks the turning point—the moment something changes. "When she opened the door, everything was different." It is the hinge on which narratives swing, the marker between before and after.

Perhaps this is why "when" resonates so deeply: it reminds us that our lives are made of moments, sequences, and turning points. We live suspended between the "whens" of our past and the "whens" we are still waiting for—between memory and anticipation, all balanced on the fragile, ever-moving point we call "now."

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style technical description of a device for measuring component mounting positional deviation in a pick-and-place machine, including nozzle and component placement sections and a fiducial mark mounting table.
counterfactuals.output:
# TECHNICAL FIELD

The present disclosure relates to a positional deviation measuring device for a pick-and-place machine (component mounting apparatus), and more particularly to a device configured to measure mounting positional deviation between an electronic component and a target substrate or carrier by utilizing a nozzle section, a component placement section, and a fiducial mark mounting table.

---

## BACKGROUND

In pick-and-place machines used for surface mount technology (SMT), electronic components are picked up from a component supply unit (e.g., tape feeder, tray feeder) by a suction nozzle mounted on a mounting head, transported over a substrate, and placed at a designated mounting position. Positional deviation between the intended mounting coordinates and the actual placed position of the component may arise due to nozzle wear, vibration during transport, camera calibration drift, thermal expansion of mechanical components, or misalignment of the fiducial marks used for coordinate referencing.

Conventional inspection methods typically rely on post-placement optical inspection (AOI) performed after the component has already been mounted on the production substrate, which does not allow correction prior to actual production and may result in defective products if deviation exceeds tolerance. There remains a need for a measuring device capable of directly and repeatably quantifying nozzle-to-placement positional deviation using a dedicated calibration mechanism integrated with the pick-and-place machine itself, independent of the production substrate.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

According to an embodiment, a component mounting positional deviation measuring device is provided, comprising:

1. A **nozzle section**, including a suction nozzle mounted to a mounting head, the nozzle section being configured to pick up an electronic component from a component supply position and to be moved by a head-driving mechanism to a component placement position;

2. A **component placement section**, disposed at a predetermined position within the pick-and-place machine, configured to receive the electronic component released from the nozzle section, the component placement section including a placement surface on which the component is mounted for subsequent position measurement;

3. A **fiducial mark mounting table**, disposed adjacent to or integrated with the component placement section, the fiducial mark mounting table having at least one fiducial mark formed thereon at a known reference coordinate, the fiducial mark mounting table being fixed relative to a machine coordinate system;

4. An **image capturing unit**, configured to simultaneously or sequentially capture images of the fiducial mark and the placed electronic component, generating combined positional image data; and

5. A **deviation calculating unit**, configured to compute a positional deviation amount between an actual mounting position of the electronic component (as determined relative to the fiducial mark) and a target mounting position stored in advance, based on the image data.

By referencing the fiducial mark mounting table—rather than relying solely on the machine's internal motion-control coordinates—the device is able to detect deviations caused by nozzle tip eccentricity, head positioning error, and camera/optics misalignment, in a manner traceable to a physically fixed reference point.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### 1. Overall Configuration

Referring to the drawings (not shown in this text description but implied per patent convention as Fig. 1 through Fig. 4), the positional deviation measuring device 100 is installed within, or removably attached to, the working area of a pick-and-place machine. The device 100 comprises a base frame 10, on which the component placement section 20 and the fiducial mark mounting table 30 are fixedly mounted in a predetermined positional relationship.

### 2. Nozzle Section

The nozzle section 40 comprises:

- A **suction nozzle 41**, having a tip opening 41a for vacuum-based pickup of an electronic component C;
- A **nozzle holder 42**, rotatably and vertically movably supported on a mounting head 43;
- A **Z-axis drive mechanism 44**, configured to move the nozzle 41 in the vertical (Z) direction for pick-up and placement operations;
- A **θ-axis rotation mechanism 45**, configured to rotate the nozzle 41 about its own axis to correct the rotational orientation of the component C prior to placement.

The mounting head 43 is movable in the X-Y plane by an XY-drive mechanism (not shown), under control of a control unit 90, such that the nozzle section 40 can transport the component C from a supply position to the component placement section 20.

### 3. Component Placement Section

The component placement section 20 comprises:

- A **placement stage 21**, having a flat upper surface 21a onto which the component C is placed by the nozzle section 40;
- Optionally, a **suction-assist mechanism 22** disposed beneath the placement surface 21a, configured to apply a slight suction force to stabilize the component C immediately after release, thereby preventing bounce or displacement due to placement impact; and
- A **surface material** selected to provide sufficient optical contrast against the component C for image recognition purposes (e.g., anti-reflective coated ceramic or matte-finished metal).

The placement stage 21 is positioned at a fixed, known coordinate (X0, Y0) relative to the base frame 10.

### 4. Fiducial Mark Mounting Table

The fiducial mark mounting table 30 comprises:

- A **table body 31**, rigidly fixed to the base frame 10 adjacent to the placement stage 21;
- One or more **fiducial marks 32** (e.g., cross-shaped, circular, or checkerboard patterns) formed on an upper surface 31a of the table body 31 by etching, printing, or laser marking, each fiducial mark 32 having a precisely known coordinate relationship to the placement stage 21;
- Optionally, a **plurality of fiducial marks 32a, 32b, 32c...** arranged at different positions surrounding the placement stage 21, to allow multi-point referencing and correction of rotational or scaling errors in the captured image (e.g., due to camera lens distortion).

The fiducial mark mounting table 30 may be formed integrally with the placement stage 21 as a single unit, or may be a separable/replaceable module to allow for periodic recalibration or replacement due to wear.

### 5. Image Capturing Unit

An image capturing unit 50, such as a CCD or CMOS camera equipped with a telecentric lens, is disposed above the component placement section 20 and fiducial mark mounting table 30. The image capturing unit 50 is configured to capture, within a single field of view or through a compositing process across multiple images, both:

(a) the position and orientation of the electronic component C placed on the placement stage 21, and
(b) the fiducial mark(s) 32 on the fiducial mark mounting table 30.

The image capturing unit 50 transmits the captured image data to an image processing unit 60.

### 6. Image Processing and Deviation Calculating Unit

The image processing unit 60 performs pattern recognition to determine:

- The center coordinates and rotational angle of the electronic component C, denoted (Xc, Yc, θc); and
- The coordinates of the fiducial mark(s) 32, denoted (Xf, Yf).

A deviation calculating unit 70 then computes the positional deviation ΔX, ΔY, and Δθ as follows:

```
ΔX = (Xc − Xf) − ΔXtarget
ΔY = (Yc − Yf) − ΔYtarget
Δθ = θc − θtarget
```

where ΔXtarget, ΔYtarget, and θtarget represent the pre-stored target relative position and orientation of the component with respect to the fiducial mark, corresponding to a zero-deviation (ideal) placement.

### 7. Control Unit and Feedback

A control unit 90, comprising a processor and memory storing target position data and calibration parameters, receives the computed deviation values from the deviation calculating unit 70. The control unit 90 may:

(a) Display the deviation values on an output device (e.g., monitor) for operator confirmation;
(b) Store the deviation values in a log for statistical process control (SPC) purposes;
(c) Automatically generate a correction offset signal, which is fed back to the XY-drive mechanism and θ-axis rotation mechanism of the mounting head 43, to compensate for the detected deviation in subsequent placement operations; and/or
(d) Trigger an alarm if the deviation exceeds a predetermined threshold, indicating a need for maintenance (e.g., nozzle replacement, camera recalibration).

### 8. Operation Sequence

The measuring operation proceeds according to the following exemplary steps:

**Step 1:** The nozzle section 40 picks up a test component C (or a dedicated calibration component) from a supply position.

**Step 2:** The mounting head 43 transports the component C to a position above the component placement section 20, based on machine coordinate data.

**Step 3:** The nozzle 41 lowers and releases the component C onto the placement stage 21.

**Step 4:** The image capturing unit 50 captures an image encompassing both the placed component C and the fiducial mark(s) 32 on the fiducial mark mounting table 30.

**Step 5:** The image processing unit 60 extracts positional data for the component C and the fiducial mark(s) 32.

**Step 6:** The deviation calculating unit 70 computes the positional deviation values ΔX, ΔY, Δθ.

**Step 7:** The control unit 90 outputs, logs, and/or feeds back correction data as described above.

**Step 8 (optional):** Steps 1–7 are repeated for a plurality of nozzles (in the case of a multi-nozzle mounting head) and/or a plurality of placement positions, to generate a comprehensive deviation map across the working range of the pick-and-place machine.

---

## ADVANTAGES

1. **Independent Reference Frame** — By providing a dedicated fiducial mark mounting table separate from the production substrate, the device enables deviation measurement without consuming production materials and without being affected by substrate-specific fiducial mark inaccuracies.

2. **Real-Time Feedback** — The feedback loop to the XY-drive and θ-axis rotation mechanisms permits real-time or near-real-time correction of subsequent placements, improving first-pass yield.

3. **Multi-Nozzle Compatibility** — The device can be used to characterize deviation across multiple nozzles of a rotary or in-line multi-head mounting system, enabling per-nozzle calibration offsets to be stored and applied individually.

4. **Wear Monitoring** — Repeated measurements over time enable trend analysis for predictive maintenance of nozzles and mechanical drive components.

5. **Modular Design** — The component placement section and fiducial mark mounting table may be provided as a replaceable cartridge, facilitating recalibration and reducing machine downtime.

---

## ALTERNATIVE EMBODIMENTS

- The fiducial mark mounting table 30 may be provided with fiducial marks made of a material readable under multiple illumination wavelengths (e.g., visible and infrared), to accommodate different camera systems.
- The component placement section 20 may include a plurality of placement stages arranged in an array, allowing simultaneous or sequential measurement at multiple locations within the machine's working area to detect systematic positional drift across the X-Y travel range.
- The image capturing unit 50 may be mounted on the mounting head 43 itself (a "head-mounted camera" configuration) rather than fixed to the base frame, in which case the fiducial mark mounting table 30 serves as a stationary reference against which the head-mounted camera's own position is calibrated.
- The suction-assist mechanism 22 may be replaced with an electrostatic or adhesive-based retention mechanism, depending on the component type.

---

## CLAIMS (Exemplary)

1. A device for measuring component mounting positional deviation in a pick-and-place machine, comprising:
 a nozzle section configured to pick up and place an electronic component;
 a component placement section configured to receive the electronic component placed by the nozzle section;
 a fiducial mark mounting table having at least one fiducial mark at a known coordinate relative to the component placement section

# ABSTRACT

A positional deviation measurement unit is configured to be removably mounted in place of a cassette-type component feeder on a component mounting machine, enabling in-situ measurement of positional deviations occurring in a component transfer path between a component supply position and a component mounting position. The measurement unit includes a base member having an external configuration and mounting interface substantially identical to that of the cassette feeder, permitting installation into an existing feeder mounting slot of the component mounting machine without modification to the machine itself.

The measurement unit further comprises one or more measurement nozzles disposed at a component supply position on the base member, the measurement nozzles being configured to be held and transferred by a mounting head of the component mounting machine in the same manner as an ordinary component held by a suction nozzle or gripping mechanism. Each measurement nozzle carries or is associated with a measurement component simulating the dimensional and positional characteristics of an actual electronic component to be mounted, such that the mounting head can pick up the measurement nozzle together with the measurement component and transport it along the normal component transfer path toward a mounting position on a circuit board or a corresponding measurement stage.

A fiducial mark is provided on the base member at a predetermined, precisely known position relative to the measurement nozzle's supply position. The fiducial mark serves as a reference point that can be optically recognized by an image recognition unit or camera provided on the component mounting machine, such as a mark camera or component recognition camera, both before and after the measurement nozzle is transferred. By capturing images of the fiducial mark and comparing the detected position of the measurement component or measurement nozzle relative to the fiducial mark at different stages of the transfer operation, a positional deviation amount arising from factors such as mounting head movement error, nozzle holding error, or image recognition error can be calculated.

The measurement unit thereby allows an operator or the machine's control system to quantitatively evaluate and calibrate positional accuracy of the component mounting machine using existing hardware, including the mounting head, recognition cameras, and control software, without requiring specialized external measurement instruments. Because the unit is installed in place of an existing cassette feeder, it is compatible with the machine's automatic feeder-exchange mechanisms and can be incorporated into routine maintenance or calibration cycles with minimal operator intervention. The disclosed configuration further supports automatic correction of mounting position data based on the measured deviation, thereby improving overall component mounting accuracy and reducing mounting defects caused by cumulative positional errors in the transfer path.

counterfactuals.output:
# Measurement Unit for Placement Position Error Detection in SMT Machines

## Overview

In SMT (Surface Mount Technology) machines, a measurement unit can be installed in place of a standard component feeder to verify and calibrate the accuracy of the pick-and-place mechanism. This unit detects the actual placement position of the mounting head relative to a known reference mark, allowing the system to measure and correct positional errors (offsets in X, Y, and θ/rotation).

## Structure

### 1. **Housing/Base Frame**
- Shaped and dimensioned to match a standard feeder so it can be mounted directly into a feeder slot on the machine's feeder bank
- Provides mechanical interface compatible with the feeder-locking mechanism

### 2. **Reference Mark (Target Plate)**
- A precision reference mark (often a cross, dot pattern, or fiducial) is embedded on the top surface of the unit
- Manufactured with high positional accuracy, serving as the "ground truth" coordinate
- Often made of a contrasting material/color to enhance optical detection

### 3. **Detection Sensor**
- **Optical Sensor/Camera**: A CCD or CMOS image sensor positioned to capture the position of a mounted component or the placement head itself relative to the reference mark
- **Light Source**: Illumination (LEDs) to ensure consistent image contrast for the sensor
- May include a **transmissive or reflective photo sensor** in simpler designs, or a **line sensor/area sensor** for more precise measurement

### 4. **Signal Processing Circuit**
- Converts sensor output (optical/analog signal) into digital position data
- Interfaces with the SMT machine's main controller via connector pins that mimic a standard feeder's communication interface

### 5. **Mechanical Alignment Features**
- Locating pins or slots ensuring the unit sits in a fixed, repeatable position within the feeder slot, matching the reference mark's known coordinates in the machine's coordinate system

## Function/Operating Principle

1. **Installation**: The measurement unit replaces a feeder in one of the feeder bank slots. Its position is precisely known relative to the machine's coordinate system.

2. **Test Placement Cycle**: The mounting head performs a placement operation as if placing a component, either:
   - Placing a dummy/test chip onto the reference mark location, or
   - Directly positioning the head/nozzle over the reference mark without a component

3. **Position Capture**: 
   - The optical sensor captures the actual landing position of the nozzle tip, suction center, or placed component relative to the embedded reference mark
   - The image processing system calculates the offset between the actual position and the ideal/target position (the reference mark)

4. **Error Calculation**:
   - Deviations in X-axis, Y-axis, and rotational (θ) alignment are computed
   - Data is sent to the machine controller

5. **Calibration/Compensation**:
   - The machine's control system uses this error data to apply correction offsets to future placement operations
   - This compensates for mechanical wear, thermal drift, backlash, or vibration-induced inaccuracies in the placement head, ball screws, or linear guides

## Purpose in the SMT Process

- **Quality Assurance**: Ensures placement accuracy meets required tolerances (often ±25–50 microns or tighter for fine-pitch components)
- **Preventive Maintenance**: Detects gradual mechanical degradation before it causes defects
- **Machine Calibration**: Used during setup, after maintenance, or periodically during production to recalibrate the placement coordinate system
- **Reduced Downtime**: Allows in-situ diagnostic testing without needing external metrology equipment

This type of unit is essentially a **built-in self-calibration tool**, leveraging the existing feeder architecture to seamlessly integrate accuracy verification into the SMT machine's operational routine.

# Formal Engineering Description: Exchangeable Feeder-Slot Calibration Device for Component Mounting Position Deviation Measurement

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This document describes the structural configuration and functional operation of an exchangeable feeder-slot device (hereinafter "calibration feeder unit") designed for use in surface-mount technology (SMT) placement machines. The device enables in-situ measurement and quantification of component mounting position deviation—encompassing translational offset (ΔX, ΔY) and rotational offset (Δθ)—by supplying reference test components to the placement head's nozzle mechanism for subsequent transfer to a calibration table equipped with position-sensing means.

## 2. General Structural Configuration

### 2.1 Feeder-Slot Interface
The calibration feeder unit is constructed as a discrete, removable module conforming to the mechanical and electrical interface standard of the host placement machine's feeder bank (feeder-slot). It comprises:

- **Base housing**: A body sized to the standard slot pitch, incorporating a locating pin/key and a locking mechanism (e.g., spring-loaded latch or cam lever) for repeatable, tool-less insertion and removal.
- **Electrical connector**: A card-edge or pin-header connector mating with the slot's backplane, providing power and communication (e.g., I²C, RS-485, or proprietary serial protocol) to the host controller.
- **Test component reservoir**: A tape-and-reel, tray, or dedicated cartridge holding a plurality of reference (dummy or gauge) components of known, calibrated dimensions and fiducial markings.
- **Component presentation mechanism**: An indexing/advance mechanism (sprocket-drive for tape, or pusher for tray-type) that positions successive test components at a fixed pickup point (the "pickup station") within the unit, analogous to conventional component feeders.

### 2.2 Positional Reference Features
The pickup station incorporates a precision-machined pocket or seating datum whose position relative to the slot's mechanical registration features is held to a specified tolerance (e.g., ±5 μm), such that the location of the test component at pickup is known with high confidence relative to the machine coordinate frame after slot registration.

## 3. Functional Description of Pickup and Placement Sequence

### 3.1 Nozzle Pickup Operation
1. The placement head, under machine motion control, is commanded to the pickup station coordinates associated with the calibration feeder unit's slot address (as recorded in the machine's slot-mapping table).
2. The mounting head's Z-axis actuator lowers the selected nozzle to the presentation plane of the test component.
3. Vacuum generation (via venturi ejector or vacuum pump, mediated by a solenoid valve) is activated, and negative pressure is applied through the nozzle's internal air passage, drawing the test component onto the nozzle tip.
4. A vacuum-pressure sensor confirms successful pickup (pressure threshold verification) prior to Z-axis retraction.
5. Optionally, the head rotates the nozzle to a reference angular orientation, and an on-head or gantry-mounted component recognition camera captures an image of the held component to determine pickup offset (nozzle-centroid vs. component-centroid deviation), which may be used as a first-stage correction value.

### 3.2 Transfer and Placement on Calibration Table
1. The placement head translates, under the machine's X-Y gantry drive, from the pickup station to the designated location of the calibration table—a fixed, high-precision reference platform mounted within the machine's working envelope (distinct from the production PCB stage).
2. The calibration table is equipped with a position-sensing subsystem, which may comprise:
   - A high-resolution vision system (downward- or upward-looking camera) referenced to the machine's global coordinate system, or
   - An embedded array of optical or capacitive position sensors beneath a transparent or perforated placement surface, or
   - A precision fiducial grid against which the placed component's position is optically measured post-placement.
3. The nozzle lowers the test component onto the calibration table at the commanded target coordinates (X_target, Y_target, θ_target).
4. Vacuum is released (and, where applicable, positive "blow-off" air pressure is briefly applied) to effect clean separation of the component from the nozzle onto the table surface.
5. The position-sensing subsystem acquires the actual placed position (X_actual, Y_actual, θ_actual) of the test component.

## 4. Deviation Computation

The control system computes the mounting position deviation vector:

$$\Delta X = X_{actual} - X_{target}$$
$$\Delta Y = Y_{actual} - Y_{target}$$
$$\Delta\theta = \theta_{actual} - \theta_{target}$$

These deviations are attributable to cumulative error sources including gantry positioning error, head/nozzle runout, pickup offset, nozzle-tip wear, and thermal drift. The computed values are used to generate correction offsets applied to subsequent production placement commands, and/or logged for statistical process control and preventive maintenance scheduling.

## 5. Repeatability Provisions

To ensure measurement validity, the calibration feeder unit and calibration table are each designed with defined mechanical repeatability specifications (e.g., ≤3 μm for the pickup pocket, ≤2 μm for the table's registration features), and the measurement cycle (Sections 3.1–3.2) may be repeated across multiple nozzles, multiple head stations, and multiple locations within the machine's working envelope to characterize spatial variation of placement accuracy across the full operating range.

---

# Patent Claim Draft: Positional Accuracy Measurement Attachment for Automated Component Placement Machines

## CLAIMS

**1.** A positional accuracy measurement attachment for an automated component placement machine, comprising:

a mounting fixture configured to be removably coupled to a placement head of the automated component placement machine, said placement head being movable along at least two orthogonal axes relative to a work surface;

an optical measurement sensor supported by said mounting fixture, said sensor configured to detect a spatial position of a reference target disposed on or proximate to said work surface;

a reference target assembly comprising at least one fiducial marker having a known geometric configuration, positioned within a field of view of said optical measurement sensor;

a data acquisition module in communication with said optical measurement sensor, configured to receive positional signals corresponding to detected coordinates of said reference target relative to said placement head; and

a processing unit configured to:
   (a) receive a commanded position corresponding to an intended placement location of said placement head;
   (b) receive said positional signals from said data acquisition module corresponding to an actual position of said placement head;
   (c) calculate a positional deviation value representing a difference between said commanded position and said actual position; and
   (d) output said positional deviation value for calibration or quality control purposes.

**2.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said optical measurement sensor comprises a machine vision camera configured to capture an image of said reference target, and wherein said processing unit is further configured to determine said actual position by image processing of said captured image.

**3.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said mounting fixture comprises a quick-release coupling mechanism enabling tool-less attachment and detachment of said measurement attachment from said placement head without requiring recalibration of the placement machine's native tooling.

**4.** The attachment of claim 1, further comprising a plurality of reference targets arranged in a predetermined grid pattern on said work surface, wherein said processing unit is configured to calculate positional deviation values at a plurality of locations across a placement envelope of said machine.

**5.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said optical measurement sensor further comprises a laser displacement sensor configured to measure a Z-axis position of said placement head relative to said work surface, and wherein said processing unit is further configured to calculate a Z-axis positional deviation value.

**6.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said processing unit is further configured to generate a correction offset value based on said positional deviation value, said correction offset value transmittable to a controller of said automated component placement machine to adjust subsequent commanded positions.

**7.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said reference target assembly comprises a plurality of fiducial markers of differing optical characteristics, enabling said optical measurement sensor to distinguish rotational orientation of said placement head in addition to said positional deviation value.

**8.** The attachment of claim 1, further comprising a temperature sensor configured to measure an ambient temperature proximate to said placement head, wherein said processing unit is further configured to apply a thermal compensation factor to said positional deviation value based on said measured ambient temperature.

**9.** The attachment of claim 1, wherein said processing unit is further configured to generate a statistical report comprising a plurality of positional deviation values collected over a plurality of placement cycles, said report indicating a repeatability metric for said automated component placement machine.

**10.** A method of measuring positional accuracy of an automated component placement machine, comprising:

removably attaching a measurement fixture to a placement head of said machine, said measurement fixture comprising an optical sensor;

commanding said placement head to move to a plurality of predetermined target positions relative to a reference target array disposed on a work surface;

capturing, via said optical sensor, positional data corresponding to an actual position of said placement head at each of said predetermined target positions;

comparing, via a processing unit, said actual position to a corresponding commanded position to generate a positional deviation value for each of said predetermined target positions; and

generating a calibration report or correction dataset based on a plurality of said positional deviation values.

**11.** The method of claim 10, further comprising applying a calculated correction offset to a motion control system of said automated component placement machine to reduce future positional deviation.

**12.** The method of claim 10, further comprising repeating said method at a plurality of time intervals to generate a trend data set indicative of mechanical wear or drift of said automated component placement machine over time.
